challenges.title: A journey starting away from the origin
challenges.question: At 08:00 a bus is 4 km along a straight road from town. It travels away at constant speed, reaching position 12 km at 08:20. It waits until 08:35, then returns at constant speed, reaching town at 09:05. (a) Find both moving speeds. (b) Find total distance and overall average speed for 08:00–09:05. (c) When does it pass its original 4 km position on return? (d) Sketch the position-time graph and state its four corners.
hints: The outward distance is 12−4, not 12 km.
Include the rest in overall time. On return, position 4 is four kilometres before the endpoint.

solution.title: Calculate moving speeds
solution.reason: Use each segment’s own distance and time.

solution.title: Calculate distance and average
solution.math: Distance=8+12=20 km; elapsed=65/60 h; average=240/13≈18.46 km/h
solution.reason: The rest lowers overall average speed.

solution.title: Locate the return crossing
solution.reason: At position 4, four kilometres remain.

solution.title: Specify graph corners
solution.reason: The initial height is 4; the rest is horizontal.

challenges.answer: (a) 24 km/h both ways. (b) 20 km; 240/13≈18.46 km/h. (c) 08:55. (d) Corners listed above.
challenges.check: Moving time is 50 minutes; 24×50/60=20 km checks total distance.

challenges.title: Does a straight cost graph mean proportion?
challenges.question: An invented equipment-hire model A charges €9 for 1 hour, €15 for 3 hours and €21 for 5 hours. Charges follow one linear rule for 0≤h≤6. Model B charges €4.50 per hour with no fee. (a) Find A’s rule and explain whether it is directly proportional. (b) Find when the prices are equal. (c) Which is cheaper at 2 hours and at 6 hours, and by how much? (d) Give two points on each graph and their common point.
hints: Find the increase per hour before the starting charge.
Equate 3h+6 and 4.5h, then compare costs on either side.

solution.title: Recover A’s rule
solution.reason: The constant slope comes with a non-zero fee.

solution.title: Test proportion
solution.math: A(0)=6, so A is not directly proportional; B(h)=4.5h is
solution.reason: A proportional graph passes through the origin.

solution.title: Find the intersection
solution.reason: Four hours is within the stated domain.

solution.title: Compare and plot
solution.reason: B saves €3 at two hours; A saves €3 at six. The common point is (4,18).

challenges.answer: (a) A=3h+6, not direct proportion. (b) 4 h at €18. (c) B saves €3 at 2 h; A saves €3 at 6 h. (d) Points listed above.
challenges.check: The unused value A(5)=21 checks the recovered rule; both models give 18 at h=4.

challenges.title: A narrow neck changes the filling graph
challenges.question: A vessel has a lower cylindrical chamber of radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Above it is a cylindrical neck of radius 2 cm and height 12 cm, beginning at water height 10 cm. Starting empty, it fills at 16π cm³/s. Ignore wall thickness. (a) Find the time to fill each part. (b) State the corners of its height-time graph until full. (c) Find the height after 11.5 s. (d) Explain the ratio of the slopes of its two graph segments.
hints: Compute each part’s volume and divide by the same inflow.
The neck has one quarter of the chamber’s area, so the level rises four times as fast.

solution.title: Find filling times
solution.math: Lower: V=160π, time=10 s. Neck: V=48π, time=3 s.
solution.reason: Each time is volume divided by 16π.

solution.title: Accumulate graph corners
solution.reason: Time and height continue across the join.

solution.title: Read the neck stage
solution.math: Neck height rate=16π/(4π)=4 cm/s; h(11.5)=10+4(1.5)=16 cm
solution.reason: Only 1.5 seconds have elapsed within the neck.

solution.title: Explain the change
solution.math: Lower slope=1 cm/s; neck slope=4 cm/s; ratio 1:4
solution.reason: At the same inflow, one quarter the area gives four times the height-rise rate.

challenges.answer: (a) 10 s and 3 s. (b) (0,0),(10,10),(13,22), joined by lines. (c) 16 cm. (d) Slopes 1:4 because areas are 4:1.
challenges.check: Total volume 208π divided by flow 16π gives 13 s, matching the last corner.

title: Algebra 2
intro: Make fractions and formulas manageable by preserving equality at every step.

lessons.title: Add algebraic fractions
lessons.goal: Build a common denominator and combine the numerators.

steps.title: Find a shared denominator
steps.text: Add x over three and x plus one over two. The smallest shared denominator is six.
steps.why: Fractions can be added directly only when they use equal-sized parts.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x/3 + (x + 1)/2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Scale both parts of each fraction
steps.text: Multiply the first numerator and denominator by two, and the second by three. Put the complete second numerator inside brackets.
steps.why: Multiplying top and bottom by the same number is multiplying by 1, so each fraction keeps its value.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x/3 + (x + 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2x/6 + 3(x + 1)/6</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Combine and expand
steps.text: Add the numerators while keeping denominator six. Distribute the three across both terms in its bracket.
steps.why: The denominator names the common part size; it is not added again.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x/3 + (x + 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x/6 + 3(x + 1)/6</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">[2x + 3(x + 1)]/6 = (5x + 3)/6</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check a simple input
steps.text: At x equal to three, the original fractions total three. The combined fraction also gives eighteen over six, which is three.
steps.why: Numerical substitution is a useful check for an algebraic identity.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x/3 + (x + 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x/6 + 3(x + 1)/6</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">[2x + 3(x + 1)]/6 = (5x + 3)/6</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = 3: 1 + 2 = 18/6 = 3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Simplify x/2 + x/3.
quiz.hint: The common denominator is six.
quiz.explanation: x/2 = 3x/6 and x/3 = 2x/6; adding gives 5x/6.

quiz.question: Which equals (x + 2)/3 − (x − 1)/2?
quiz.hint: Subtract the entire second numerator after scaling.

lessons.takeaway: Use common-sized parts, keep whole numerators in brackets, then combine.
lessons.mistake: Adding denominators or subtracting only the first term of a numerator.

lessons.title: Cancel factors, not terms
lessons.goal: Simplify variable fractions and preserve excluded values.

steps.title: Record the forbidden input
steps.text: Simplify x squared minus nine over x minus three. The original denominator is zero at x equal to three, so that input is excluded.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined, even if later cancellation hides the denominator.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(x² − 9)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Factorise the numerator
steps.text: The numerator is a difference of squares. It becomes x minus three times x plus three.
steps.why: Factorisation reveals whole common factors that can cancel.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3)</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Divide out the common factor
steps.text: For allowed inputs, the factor x minus three is non-zero and divides itself to give one. The remaining factor is x plus three.
steps.why: Cancellation is division by the same non-zero factor in numerator and denominator.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">[(x − 3)(x + 3)]/(x − 3) = x + 3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Keep the restriction attached
steps.text: The simplified expression still describes the original only when x is not three. For x equal to five, both versions give eight.
steps.why: Algebraic simplification cannot enlarge the original domain without saying so.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">[(x − 3)(x + 3)]/(x − 3) = x + 3</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x + 3, x ≠ 3; at x = 5 → 8</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Simplify (x² − 4)/(x − 2).
quiz.hint: Factorise the difference of squares and keep the original restriction.
quiz.explanation: (x²−4) = (x−2)(x+2), so the result is x+2 with x ≠ 2.

quiz.question: Can x be cancelled from (x + 5)/x?
options: No; x is not a factor of the whole numerator
quiz.hint: Cancellation requires a common factor, not a term inside a sum.
quiz.explanation: (x+5)/x = 1 + 5/x for x ≠ 0. It does not simplify to 5 or 6.

lessons.takeaway: Factorise first, cancel whole non-zero factors, retain restrictions.
lessons.mistake: Crossing out a term inside a sum.

lessons.title: Multiply algebraic fractions
lessons.goal: Factorise, record restrictions and cancel across a product.

steps.title: Record the original denominators
steps.text: Multiply x squared minus nine over twice x by x over x plus three. The original denominators exclude zero and negative three.
steps.why: Every original denominator must remain non-zero.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(x² − 9)/(2x) × x/(x + 3); x ≠ 0, −3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Factorise before cancelling
steps.text: Rewrite x squared minus nine as x minus three times x plus three. A product of fractions forms one product above one product below.
steps.why: Only complete factors may cancel across a fraction bar.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(2x) × x/(x + 3); x ≠ 0, −3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">[(x − 3)(x + 3)x]/[2x(x + 3)]</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Cancel matching non-zero factors
steps.text: The factor x cancels, as does x plus three. These cancellations are valid because those factors are non-zero for every allowed input.
steps.why: A non-zero factor divided by itself is one.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(2x) × x/(x + 3); x ≠ 0, −3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">[(x − 3)(x + 3)x]/[2x(x + 3)]</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">result = (x − 3)/2, x ≠ 0, −3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check a permitted value
steps.text: At x equal to five, the first fraction is sixteen tenths and the second is five eighths. Their product and the simplified expression both equal one.
steps.why: A check confirms the arithmetic but does not remove the domain restrictions.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 9)/(2x) × x/(x + 3); x ≠ 0, −3</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">[(x − 3)(x + 3)x]/[2x(x + 3)]</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">result = (x − 3)/2, x ≠ 0, −3</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(16/10)(5/8) = 1 = (5 − 3)/2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Simplify (3x/4) × (8/x), with x ≠ 0.
quiz.hint: Multiply the numerators and denominators, then cancel x.
quiz.explanation: 24x/(4x) = 6 when x is non-zero.

quiz.question: Which restriction is needed before simplifying (x²−1)/(x+1)?
quiz.hint: Set the original denominator equal to zero.
quiz.explanation: The denominator x+1 is zero at x = −1. The simplified expression x−1 retains that exclusion.

lessons.takeaway: Multiply factors, cancel common non-zero factors, and retain original exclusions.
lessons.mistake: Cancelling a piece of a sum before factorising the whole expression.

lessons.title: Divide algebraic fractions
lessons.goal: Invert the divisor while keeping its non-zero condition.

steps.title: Identify the divisor and all exclusions
steps.text: Divide x squared minus four over three x by x plus two over six. The first denominator excludes zero; the divisor itself must not be zero, so x cannot be negative two.
steps.why: Division requires a defined, non-zero divisor.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(x² − 4)/(3x) ÷ (x + 2)/6; x ≠ 0, −2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Multiply by the reciprocal
steps.text: Keep the first fraction unchanged. Turn the divisor over and change division to multiplication.
steps.why: Dividing by a non-zero fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, so the value is unchanged.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 4)/(3x) ÷ (x + 2)/6; x ≠ 0, −2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(x² − 4)/(3x) × 6/(x + 2)</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Factorise and simplify
steps.text: Factorise the difference of squares and cancel x plus two. Divide six by three to obtain two.
steps.why: Cancellation is valid on the restricted domain recorded at the start.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 4)/(3x) ÷ (x + 2)/6; x ≠ 0, −2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 4)/(3x) × 6/(x + 2)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">[(x − 2)(x + 2)6]/[3x(x + 2)] = 2(x − 2)/x</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check the division directly
steps.text: At x equal to four, the first fraction is one and the divisor is one, so their quotient is one. The simplified fraction also gives one; both exclusions still apply.
steps.why: Checking the original division catches an accidentally inverted first fraction.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 4)/(3x) ÷ (x + 2)/6; x ≠ 0, −2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x² − 4)/(3x) × 6/(x + 2)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">[(x − 2)(x + 2)6]/[3x(x + 2)] = 2(x − 2)/x</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2(4 − 2)/4 = 1; x ≠ 0, −2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Simplify (x/3) ÷ (2/5).
quiz.hint: Keep x/3 and multiply by 5/2.

quiz.question: When dividing by (x−1)/4, which extra value is forbidden because the divisor would be zero?
quiz.hint: The divisor is zero when its numerator is zero.
quiz.explanation: At x = 1, (x−1)/4 = 0. Division by that value is undefined.

lessons.takeaway: Keep the first fraction; invert the divisor; factor and cancel; keep all exclusions.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting that the divisor cannot be zero, even when its denominator is safe.

lessons.title: Add fractions with variable denominators
lessons.goal: Build a denominator that contains every required factor.

steps.title: Identify denominators and excluded inputs
steps.text: Add two over x to three over x plus one. The input cannot be zero or negative one.
steps.why: Denominators define the original restrictions before any simplification.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2/x + 3/(x + 1); x ≠ 0, −1</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Build equal denominators
steps.text: Use x times x plus one as the common denominator. Multiply top and bottom of the first fraction by x plus one, and top and bottom of the second by x.
steps.why: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same non-zero factor preserves a fraction.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2/x + 3/(x + 1); x ≠ 0, −1</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2(x + 1)/[x(x + 1)] + 3x/[x(x + 1)]</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Combine whole numerators
steps.text: Add two times x plus one and three x, then expand. Keep the common denominator unchanged.
steps.why: Once part sizes match, only the counts in the numerator are added.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2/x + 3/(x + 1); x ≠ 0, −1</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2(x + 1)/[x(x + 1)] + 3x/[x(x + 1)]</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#087f75">[2(x + 1) + 3x]/[x(x + 1)] = (5x + 2)/[x(x + 1)]</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check and preserve restrictions
steps.text: At x equal to two, the original sum is one plus one, which is two. The combined fraction gives twelve over six, also two.
steps.why: Substitution confirms the algebra. Since 5x + 2 shares no factor with x or x + 1, nothing cancels, and x ≠ 0, −1 stays attached.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2/x + 3/(x + 1); x ≠ 0, −1</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2(x + 1)/[x(x + 1)] + 3x/[x(x + 1)]</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">[2(x + 1) + 3x]/[x(x + 1)] = (5x + 2)/[x(x + 1)]</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = 2: 2/2 + 3/3 = 12/6 = 2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Combine 1/x + 1/(x+2), with x ≠ 0, −2.
quiz.hint: Use the product x(x+2) as a common denominator.
quiz.explanation: The new numerator is (x+2)+x = 2x+2. The denominator stays x(x+2).

quiz.question: Which is the smallest common denominator for 1/x and 1/x², with x ≠ 0?
quiz.hint: It must contain enough factors of x for each denominator.
quiz.explanation: x² contains both required powers. Multiply the first fraction by x/x; the second already has denominator x².

lessons.takeaway: Factorise denominators, choose their common multiple, scale whole numerators, then combine.
lessons.mistake: Adding denominators or cancelling an x from only part of a numerator.

lessons.title: Clear fractions in an equation
lessons.goal: Multiply every term by a common denominator.

steps.title: Find the common multiplier
steps.text: Solve x plus one over three equals x minus one over two. Six is a multiple of both denominators.
steps.why: A common denominator lets one multiplication clear every fraction.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(x + 1)/3 = (x − 1)/2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Multiply both complete sides
steps.text: Multiply both sides by six. The left denominator divides six to give two, and the right gives three.
steps.why: Equality is preserved when both sides are multiplied by the same non-zero number.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x + 1)/3 = (x − 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2(x + 1) = 3(x − 1)</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Expand and collect
steps.text: Expand both brackets. Subtract 2x from both sides and add 3 to both sides, leaving x equal to five.
steps.why: Expanding brackets and doing the same to both sides keep every new line equivalent to the one before.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x + 1)/3 = (x − 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2(x + 1) = 3(x − 1)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2x + 2 = 3x − 3 → x = 5</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check in the original fractions
steps.text: Substitute five before declaring the solution. Both sides become two, so the original equality holds.
steps.why: The original equation is the final test.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">(x + 1)/3 = (x − 1)/2</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2(x + 1) = 3(x − 1)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x + 2 = 3x − 3 → x = 5</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">(5 + 1)/3 = (5 − 1)/2 = 2</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Solve x/3 + 2 = 5.
quiz.hint: Subtract 2 before multiplying by 3.

quiz.question: Multiplying x/2 + 3 = 7 by 2 gives…
quiz.hint: The multiplier applies to every term on both sides.

lessons.takeaway: The common multiplier applies to every term, including whole numbers.
lessons.mistake: Multiplying the fractions but forgetting the un-fractioned terms.

lessons.title: Translate a fraction word problem
lessons.goal: Name the whole, translate each part and check the context.

steps.title: Define the unknown whole
steps.text: A student spends one third of his money, then spends another five euro. He has thirteen euro left; let x be his starting amount.
steps.why: A clear definition fixes the meaning of the variable.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = starting money in euro</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Write the remaining amount
steps.text: After spending one third, two thirds of the original remains. Subtract the extra five euro to represent the amount left.
steps.why: Whole minus one third leaves two thirds.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x = starting money in euro</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2x/3 − 5 = 13</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Solve without changing the story
steps.text: Add five to both sides, then multiply by three and divide by two. The starting amount is twenty-seven euro.
steps.why: Each reverse operation undoes a change to the remaining amount.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x = starting money in euro</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x/3 − 5 = 13</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">2x/3 = 18 → 2x = 54 → x = 27</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check the actual spending
steps.text: One third of twenty-seven is nine. Spending nine and then five leaves thirteen, as the story requires.
steps.why: A contextual check confirms both the algebra and the interpretation.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x = starting money in euro</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x/3 − 5 = 13</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">2x/3 = 18 → 2x = 54 → x = 27</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">27 − 9 − 5 = 13</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: A person spends one quarter of €x and has €18 left. The equation is…
quiz.hint: Three quarters remains after spending one quarter.
quiz.explanation: The remaining amount is x − x/4 = 3x/4, which equals 18.

quiz.question: Half a number plus 7 is 19. The number is…
quiz.hint: Subtract 7, then undo halving.

lessons.takeaway: Define the whole first; translate the fraction as a fraction of that whole.
lessons.mistake: Taking a fraction of the wrong amount.

lessons.title: Change the subject of a formula
lessons.goal: Undo operations and isolate a chosen variable.

steps.title: Choose the variable to isolate
steps.text: The formula y equals three x plus five gives y directly. To calculate x from y, make x the subject instead.
steps.why: Changing the subject rewrites the same relationship.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">y = 3x + 5</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Undo the outer addition
steps.text: Subtract five from both sides. Keep the whole expression y minus five together.
steps.why: The addition happened last, so it is undone first.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = 3x + 5</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">y − 5 = 3x</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Undo the multiplication
steps.text: Divide both complete sides by three. The entire numerator y minus five is divided by three.
steps.why: Division by the same non-zero number preserves equality.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = 3x + 5</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y − 5 = 3x</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = (y − 5)/3</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Use and check the rearrangement
steps.text: If y is twenty, the rearranged formula gives x equal to five. Substituting five into the original formula returns twenty.
steps.why: A reverse calculation checks the new subject formula.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = 3x + 5</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y − 5 = 3x</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x = (y − 5)/3</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = (20 − 5)/3 = 5; 3(5) + 5 = 20</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Make h the subject of A = bh/2, where b ≠ 0.
quiz.hint: Multiply by 2, then divide by b.
quiz.explanation: 2A = bh, so h = 2A/b.

quiz.question: From v = u + at, with a ≠ 0, t equals…
quiz.hint: Undo addition of u, then multiplication by a.
quiz.explanation: v − u = at, so t = (v − u)/a. The brackets include the whole numerator.

lessons.takeaway: Undo operations from the outside in, keeping grouped expressions intact.
lessons.mistake: Dividing only one term of a multi-term numerator.

lessons.title: When the subject appears twice
lessons.goal: Collect and factor the target variable before dividing.

steps.title: Spot the repeated subject
steps.text: Make x the subject of y equals a x plus b x. There are two x terms, so do not try to divide each one separately.
steps.why: A common factor can be taken out of the complete right side.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">y = ax + bx</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Take out the subject as a common factor
steps.text: Both terms contain x. Factorising produces x multiplied by the sum of a and b.
steps.why: Factorising is expanding in reverse: x(a + b) expands back to ax + bx.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = ax + bx</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">y = x(a + b)</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Divide by its whole coefficient
steps.text: Divide by the bracket a plus b, provided it is not zero. This leaves x alone.
steps.why: Division is valid only by a non-zero quantity.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = ax + bx</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = x(a + b)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = y/(a + b), a + b ≠ 0</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Check the regrouping numerically
steps.text: For a equal to two, b equal to three and y equal to twenty, x is four. Both original terms then add to twenty.
steps.why: A check must use the original unfactored relationship.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = ax + bx</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">y = x(a + b)</text><rect id="row-2" x="45" y="209" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-2" x="380" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">x = y/(a + b), a + b ≠ 0</text><rect id="row-3" x="45" y="286" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-3" x="380" y="325" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">x = 20/(2 + 3) = 4; 2(4) + 3(4) = 20</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

quiz.question: Make x the subject of P = 2x + kx, where k ≠ −2.
quiz.hint: Take x out as a common factor before dividing.

quiz.question: Which restriction is needed to divide by a − b?
quiz.hint: The divisor must not be zero.
quiz.explanation: a − b ≠ 0 is equivalent to a ≠ b. It may be positive or negative.

lessons.takeaway: Collect the subject, factor it, then divide by the entire coefficient.
lessons.mistake: Dividing by one coefficient while another subject term remains.

lessons.title: Build and evaluate a formula
lessons.goal: Describe a situation with a rule, then substitute with units.

steps.title: Identify fixed and changing parts
steps.text: A training session costs a fixed twelve euro plus four euro per player. Let n be the number of players and C the total cost in euro.
steps.why: The fixed part is paid once; the changing part repeats for each player.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">C = 12 + 4n</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Substitute the complete value
steps.text: For seven players, put seven in place of n and perform multiplication first.
steps.why: Order of operations keeps the per-player charge grouped correctly.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">C = 12 + 4n</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">C = 12 + 4(7) = 40</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Use the formula backwards
steps.text: If the total is sixty euro, subtract the fixed charge before dividing by the per-player charge.
steps.why: Only the amount above the fixed charge comes from the players.

steps.title: Respect the allowed inputs
steps.text: A player count is a non-negative whole number. If rearrangement gives a fractional player, the data do not describe an exact total under this pricing rule.
steps.why: Context restricts the domain even when algebra permits more values.

quiz.question: A taxi model charges €5 plus €2 per kilometre d. Its cost formula is…
quiz.hint: Separate the once-only charge from the repeated charge.
quiz.explanation: The €5 is fixed and €2 is charged d times: C = 5 + 2d.

quiz.question: For C = 12 + 4n, a cost of €44 corresponds to…
quiz.hint: Remove the fixed €12 first.

lessons.takeaway: Define variables and units, separate fixed and variable parts, then test the rule.
lessons.mistake: Multiplying a fixed fee by the number of people.

reference.name: Add fractions
reference.note: B and D must be non-zero; use the LCM when possible.

reference.name: Subtract fractions
reference.note: Keep brackets around a multi-term numerator being subtracted.

reference.name: Clear denominators
reference.formula: Multiply EVERY term by a common multiple
reference.note: Record any values excluded by the original denominators.

reference.name: Change the subject
reference.formula: Apply the same reversible operation to both sides
reference.note: If the subject appears twice, collect its terms and take it out as a common factor.

reference.name: Multiply fractions
reference.note: B and D must be non-zero. Factorise before cancelling; keep all original restrictions.

reference.name: Divide fractions
reference.note: B, C and D must be non-zero: the divisor must be defined and must not equal zero.

toolkit.strategy: Before manipulating anything, record forbidden denominators and define what each variable measures. Decide whether you are simplifying an expression, solving an equation or changing a subject.

methods.title: Add or subtract algebraic fractions
methods.when: Fractions with unlike numerical or variable denominators are combined.
methods.rule: A/B ± C/D=(AD±BC)/(BD), B,D≠0; use a smaller common denominator when possible.
steps: Factorise denominators and record exclusions.
Choose a common multiple of all factors.
Scale complete numerators, keeping subtraction brackets.
Combine and simplify factors only.
methods.check: At x=1 both versions give zero.
methods.trap: Subtracting only the first term of a bracketed numerator.

methods.title: Multiply fractions by cancelling factors
methods.when: A product of rational expressions needs simplification.
methods.rule: (A/B)(C/D)=AC/(BD); only common non-zero factors cancel.
steps: Record all original restrictions.
Factorise numerators and denominators.
Cancel complete matching factors across the product.
Keep exclusions beside the result.
methods.check: At x=3 the product is 1, matching the simplified form.
methods.trap: Cancelling terms inside a sum.

methods.title: Divide fractions and preserve divisor restrictions
methods.when: One rational expression is divided by another.
methods.rule: (A/B)÷(C/D)=(A/B)(D/C), with B,D≠0 and C≠0.
steps: Exclude zeros of both original denominators and of the divisor numerator.
Keep the first fraction and invert only the divisor.
Factorise and cancel.
State the original exclusions even if factors disappear.
methods.check: Multiplying the result by the original divisor returns the first fraction on the allowed domain.
methods.trap: Checking denominator restrictions but forgetting division by zero.

methods.title: Substitute fractional or negative values
methods.when: A simplified expression or formula is evaluated at a non-integer input.
methods.rule: Substitute the whole value in brackets; division by a fraction multiplies by its reciprocal.
steps: Check that the input is allowed.
Evaluate numerator and denominator separately with exact fractions.
Divide only after both have been simplified.
methods.check: Multiply −4/3 by denominator 3/2 to recover numerator −2.
methods.trap: Treating division by 3/2 as multiplication by 3/2.

methods.title: Solve equations containing fractions
methods.when: An equality contains fractional terms.
methods.rule: Multiply both complete sides by the least common denominator; variable factors used must be non-zero.
steps: Record domain restrictions first.
Multiply every term on both sides by the common denominator.
Expand, collect and solve.
Check candidates in the original equation.
methods.check: Original sides give 3/3−0/2=1.
methods.trap: Multiplying only one term on a side.

methods.title: Build a fraction word equation
methods.when: Amounts are spent, removed or compared in fractional parts.
methods.rule: A fraction p of an amount X is pX; the remainder is (1−p)X.
steps: Name the original unknown amount.
Translate each event in order.
Set the final expression equal to the stated outcome.
Solve and replay the story numerically.
methods.example: After spending 2/5 of x and then €6, €18 remains: (3/5)x−6=18 → x=40.
methods.trap: Applying every fraction to the original amount regardless of the event order.

methods.title: Track successive transfers between two people
methods.when: A later transfer is a fraction of an amount changed by an earlier transfer.
methods.rule: Update both balances after each transfer; total money is conserved if nothing enters or leaves.
steps: Make a two-column balance table.
Apply the first fraction to its stated current balance.
Recalculate both balances before the next fraction.
Use the final comparison to form an equation.
methods.example: If A starts with x and B with 30, A gives x/4: balances 3x/4 and 30+x/4. A later fraction of B uses 30+x/4.
methods.check: The two balance expressions must always sum to x+30.
methods.trap: Taking B’s later transfer as a fraction of the original 30 only.

methods.title: Change a simple subject
methods.when: The required variable appears once.
methods.rule: Undo operations in reverse order, keeping equality; division by a coefficient requires it to be non-zero.
steps: Identify the variable to isolate.
Undo outer additions before multiplication or division.
Clear a denominator or power when necessary, respecting any domain condition.
methods.example: v=u+at gives t=(v−u)/a for a≠0.
methods.check: Substituting into u+at returns v.
methods.trap: Changing signs by a slogan without applying the same operation to both sides.

methods.title: Collect a subject that appears more than once
methods.when: The required variable occurs in several terms.
methods.rule: ax+bx=x(a+b); isolate by factoring, then divide only if the factor is non-zero.
steps: Expand brackets if needed.
Bring all subject terms to one side and other terms to the other.
Take the subject out as a common factor.
Divide by its remaining factor and state the condition.
methods.example: y=ax−c+bx gives x=(y+c)/(a+b), a+b≠0.
methods.check: Insert the result into (a+b)x−c to recover y.
methods.trap: Trying to isolate two copies of x independently.

methods.title: Subject in numerator and denominator
methods.when: A variable appears both above and below a fraction bar.
methods.rule: If y=(ax+b)/(cx+d), then x=(b−dy)/(cy−a), provided original cx+d≠0 and cy−a≠0; exceptional cases must be checked.
steps: Record the original forbidden x.
Multiply by the whole denominator.
Collect every x term on one side and factor x.
Divide by its coefficient and examine any excluded y separately.
methods.example: y=(2x+1)/(x−3) gives x=(3y+1)/(y−2), with x≠3 and y≠2.
methods.check: For y=0, x=−1/2 makes the original numerator zero while the denominator remains non-zero.
methods.trap: Dividing by an expression that could be zero without checking that case.

methods.title: Build formulas from combined shapes
methods.when: Lengths are algebraic and the perimeter or area of a joined/cut shape is given.
methods.rule: Perimeter counts the exposed boundary; area adds component areas or subtracts removed areas. All physical lengths must be positive.
steps: Label every boundary segment, including new edges at cut-outs.
Write dimension constraints before solving.
Collect a perimeter or area expression.
Solve for the requested variable and verify the actual dimensions.
methods.example: Removing a corner rectangle from an outer W-by-H rectangle leaves perimeter 2W+2H when the two new edges replace equal removed lengths.
methods.check: Trace the entire boundary once; do not count internal joins.
methods.trap: Subtracting the cut-out perimeter from the outer perimeter.

methods.title: Use a formula and reverse it within its domain
methods.when: A rule models prices, lengths or measurements.
methods.rule: Substitution evaluates the rule; reversing solves an equation. A model’s domain may be narrower than all real numbers.
steps: State what the variable and units mean.
Evaluate with exact inputs.
For a target output, solve and then apply the practical constraints.
methods.example: P=4x+18 with x>2 gives x=(P−18)/4 and requires P>26.
methods.check: A proposed x must produce the requested P and satisfy x>2.
methods.trap: Keeping an algebraic answer that makes a physical length non-positive.

checks: Keep all original denominator exclusions, including any zero divisor in fraction division.
Multiply every term when clearing denominators.
Apply each transfer fraction to the amount at that moment.
Substitute into the original formula or story to check; a transformed line alone is not enough.
Reject values that violate positive dimensions or the meaning of a quantity.

challenges.title: A subject on both sides of the fraction bar
challenges.question: The formula is y=(3x+4)/(2x−5). (a) State the forbidden value of x. (b) Make x the subject and state any forbidden value of y. (c) Find x exactly when y=2/3. (d) Explain directly from the original formula why y=3/2 is impossible.
hints: Multiply y by the complete denominator before collecting x terms.
You should obtain x(2y−3)=5y+4; test the case 2y−3=0 separately.

solution.title: Record the original restriction
solution.reason: The original denominator must exist.

solution.title: Collect the subject
solution.reason: All x terms are gathered before factorising.

solution.title: Divide and evaluate
solution.reason: A zero coefficient cannot be divided out.

solution.title: Check the exceptional output
solution.reason: There is no original input producing that output.

challenges.answer: (a) x≠5/2. (b) x=(5y+4)/(2y−3), y≠3/2. (c) x=−22/5. (d) It produces a contradiction.
challenges.check: At x=−22/5, the original numerator is −46/5 and denominator −69/5; their quotient is 2/3.

challenges.title: A division that hides several restrictions
challenges.question: Simplify E(x)=[(x²−16)/(x²+7x+12)] ÷ [(x−4)/(2x)]. (a) List every value excluded by the original expression, including values that make the divisor zero. (b) Simplify E(x). (c) Evaluate E(1/2) exactly. (d) Explain why the simplified rule cannot be used to assign a value to the original expression at x=4.
hints: Factorise both quadratics before cancelling.
The original denominator factors are (x+3)(x+4) and 2x; also exclude the zero of x−4.

solution.title: Record all restrictions
solution.reason: The first three exclusions come from denominators; x=4 makes the divisor zero.

solution.title: Invert the divisor and factor
solution.reason: Division changes to multiplication by the divisor’s reciprocal.

solution.title: Cancel complete non-zero factors
solution.reason: Cancellation does not expand the original domain.

solution.title: Substitute and interpret
solution.math: E(1/2)=1/(7/2)=2/7; x=4 remains undefined in the original
solution.reason: The apparent value 8/7 at x=4 belongs only to an extended simplified rule, not the original division.

challenges.answer: (a) Exclude −3,−4,0,4. (b) 2x/(x+3), with those exclusions. (c) 2/7. (d) The original divisor is zero at 4.
challenges.check: At x=1/2 the first fraction is −1 and the divisor is −7/2, giving (−1)÷(−7/2)=2/7 independently.

challenges.title: A cut-out shape and its allowable dimensions
challenges.question: An outer rectangle has width x+8 cm and height x+5 cm. Remove a rectangle from its top-right corner, of width 3 cm and height x−1 cm. The removed rectangle must have positive dimensions and fit strictly within the outer width and height. (a) Find the strongest resulting lower bound on x. (b) Derive the remaining shape’s perimeter P. (c) If P=50 cm, find x and the area of the remaining shape. (d) Make x the subject of P and state the corresponding condition on P.
hints: The new inside horizontal and vertical edges replace removed outer lengths of the same size.
For area, subtract 3(x−1) from (x+8)(x+5).

solution.title: Apply physical constraints
solution.reason: Positive cut-out height is the most restrictive condition.

solution.title: Trace the boundary
solution.reason: At a corner cut-out, removed outer lengths reappear as new exposed edges.

solution.title: Find the dimensions
solution.reason: This lies within x>1.

solution.title: Subtract the removed area
solution.reason: The removed rectangle’s area, not its perimeter, is subtracted.

solution.title: Reverse with its domain
solution.reason: The rearranged formula retains the physical constraints.

challenges.answer: (a) x>1. (b) P=4x+26 cm. (c) x=6; area 139 cm². (d) x=(P−26)/4 with P>30 cm.
challenges.check: At x=6 the outer rectangle is 14 by 11 and the cut-out is 3 by 5: area 154−15=139; boundary lengths total 50.

challenges.title: Fractions of changed balances
challenges.question: Ava starts with €x and Ben with €48. Ava gives Ben one third of her starting money. Ben then gives Ava one quarter of the amount he now has. Afterwards Ava has €18 more than Ben. No money enters or leaves their combined total. (a) Write both balances after each transfer. (b) Find x. (c) Find their final balances. (d) What fraction of their combined money does Ava finally hold?
hints: Update Ben’s balance before taking its quarter.
After the first transfer Ben has 48+x/3; his return transfer is (48+x/3)/4.

solution.title: Record the first transfer
solution.reason: The transfer is one third of Ava’s starting amount.

solution.title: Update both balances again
solution.reason: The quarter is taken from Ben’s new balance.

solution.title: Use the final difference
solution.reason: Ava’s final balance exceeds Ben’s by 18.

solution.title: Replay the transfers
solution.math: After first: Ava 56, Ben 76. Return transfer 19. Final: Ava 75, Ben 57.
solution.reason: Numerical replay checks the original sequence of events.

solution.title: Find the final share
solution.reason: Ava’s share is measured against the unchanged combined total.

challenges.answer: (a) Balances above. (b) x=84. (c) Ava has €75 and Ben has €57. (d) Ava holds 25/44 of the combined amount.
challenges.check: 75+57=132=84+48 and 75−57=18, checking conservation and the final condition.

title: Trigonometry
intro: Choose the correct sides and ratio, then solve one clear equation.

lessons.title: Use Pythagoras in either direction
lessons.goal: Choose addition or subtraction by identifying the hypotenuse.

steps.title: Find the hypotenuse first
steps.text: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse lies opposite the right angle. Here the shorter sides are six and eight units.
steps.why: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, so its square equals the sum of the squares on the two shorter sides.

steps.title: Add the two smaller squares
steps.text: Squaring gives thirty-six and sixty-four. Their sum is one hundred.
steps.why: Pythagoras relates areas of squares on the three sides.

steps.title: Take the positive square root
steps.text: The length is ten units. Use the positive root because a side length cannot be negative.
steps.why: Squaring and taking a non-negative square root are inverse operations for lengths.

steps.title: Subtract when a shorter side is missing
steps.text: If the hypotenuse is ten and one shorter side is eight, subtract sixty-four from one hundred. Then take the square root to recover the other side.
steps.why: Rearrange the same equation instead of always adding.

quiz.question: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 5 and 12. Its hypotenuse is…
quiz.hint: Add the squares and then square-root.

quiz.question: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 and one shorter side 5. The other side is…
quiz.hint: Subtract the known shorter-side square from the hypotenuse square.

lessons.takeaway: Longest side missing: add squares. Shorter side missing: subtract from the longest-side square.
lessons.mistake: Using Pythagoras without a right angle, or forgetting the final square root.

lessons.title: Name the sides and choose a ratio
lessons.goal: Use SOH CAH TOA as three equations, not a guess.

steps.title: Mark the angle you are using
steps.text: Sides called opposite and adjacent depend on the chosen angle. The hypotenuse is fixed by the right angle.
steps.why: Changing the reference angle swaps the two shorter-side names.
steps.math: H = side opposite the right angle

steps.title: Name opposite and adjacent
steps.text: The opposite side is across from the marked angle. The adjacent side touches that angle but is not the hypotenuse.
steps.why: These two descriptions identify the shorter sides without relying on page orientation.
steps.math: O = across from θ; A = beside θ

steps.title: Match the available pair
steps.text: With opposite six and hypotenuse ten, use sine. With adjacent eight and hypotenuse ten, use cosine; opposite and adjacent use tangent.
steps.why: Choose the ratio containing the known and required sides.
steps.math: sin θ = 6/10; cos θ = 8/10; tan θ = 6/8

steps.title: Check the ratio is plausible
steps.text: Sine and cosine of an acute angle are between zero and one because a shorter side is divided by the hypotenuse. Tangent can exceed one.
steps.why: The hypotenuse is longer than either shorter side.

quiz.question: Which ratio uses opposite and adjacent sides?
quiz.hint: SOH, CAH, TOA.
quiz.explanation: TOA means tan θ = opposite/adjacent. Sine and cosine each involve the hypotenuse, so neither uses only these two sides.

quiz.question: The hypotenuse is…
options: Always opposite the marked acute angle
Any side touching the marked angle
quiz.hint: Locate the 90° corner.
quiz.explanation: The hypotenuse lies opposite the right angle, regardless of orientation.

lessons.takeaway: Mark θ, label O/A/H, then choose the ratio containing the sides you need.
lessons.mistake: Calling the hypotenuse the adjacent side because it touches the angle.

lessons.title: Use the calculator without losing meaning
lessons.goal: Find ratios and angles in degree mode.

steps.title: Set degrees before calculating
steps.text: The angles in these exercises are measured in degrees. Check that the calculator shows DEG before using sine, cosine or tangent.
steps.why: In RAD (radian) mode the calculator treats 30 as a different unit of angle, so sin 30 would not give 0.5.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">DEG mode; sin 30° = 0.5</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Use a ratio to find an angle
steps.text: If opposite is six and hypotenuse is ten, sine of the angle equals zero point six. Now ask which acute angle has that sine.
steps.why: Inverse sine reverses the sine operation on the acute-angle range.
steps.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 400" role="img"><rect x="0" y="0" width="760" height="400" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2"/><rect id="row-0" x="45" y="55" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#f3f6fa" stroke="#dce5eb" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-0" x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#173349">DEG mode; sin 30° = 0.5</text><rect id="row-1" x="45" y="132" width="670" height="62" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text id="eq-1" x="380" y="171" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#087f75">sin θ = 6/10 = 0.6</text><text id="caption" x="380" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#8ca1af">Read the highlighted line, then explain why it follows.</text></svg>

steps.title: Apply inverse sine
steps.text: Use the inverse-sine key on zero point six. The angle is approximately thirty-six point nine degrees.
steps.why: Inverse trig returns an angle, so its answer needs an angle unit.

steps.title: Check and round only at the end
steps.text: Substituting the unrounded angle into sine should return zero point six. Keep full calculator precision during intermediate work.
steps.why: Premature rounding can change the final length or angle.
